contentModes.info-en: Lesson Info ✕ OBJECTIVE 2.4 Dashboards, Scorecards & Reports What you'll learn Distinguish dashboards, scorecards and reports by the question they answer. Read the source scorecard and communicate uncertainty, including its unit discrepancy. Slides 1–6 — Full explanations Slide 1 — A dashboard makes status and trends visible. A dashboard makes status and trends visible. Choose visual evidence that answers a security question, with a date and a defined scope. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Current security status Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Security incidents Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Vulnerability levels Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Patch compliance Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Risk trends Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. A security dashboard provides a visual representation of cybersecurity information and metrics. The source lists current security status, security incidents, vulnerability levels, patch compliance and risk trends, using charts, graphs, tables or trend indicators. An authored example shows overdue critical findings decreasing from 12 to 8 to 5 across three equal reporting periods; this is a count, not a percentage, and does not alone prove lower overall risk. Define the cohort and investigate missing coverage or changed definitions before interpreting it. A dashboard is not necessarily real time: display its update time and data limitations. For the official AI application, a model-drift KRI can appear alongside other measures, with the model/version, reference population, observation window and responsible reviewer identified. A drift signal prompts validation; it is not automatic proof of an attack or failure. Use a chart, graph, table or trend indicator that supports the question. Keep units, periods and definitions consistent before comparing. Show missing or stale data rather than implying a healthy state. Visible information still needs interpretation. Slide 2 — A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. Source example: Patch Compliance — target 95%, actual 91%, Needs Improvement. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Compare actual performance against targets Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Track progress Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Identify areas of concern Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Communicate performance to management Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Support accountability Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. A security scorecard summarizes performance against predefined objectives or targets. It helps compare actual performance, track progress, identify concerns, communicate to management and support accountability. In the course example, patch compliance has a target of 95% and actual 91%, so it needs improvement against that target: a gap of 4 percentage points, not 4% relative change. These are illustrative organizational values, not ISC 2 requirements or universal thresholds. The target and actual must refer to the same measure, period and population; show the owner and follow-up so a status can lead to action. A scorecard may use colours but should also provide explicit text. Meeting one target does not establish that every critical asset is protected or that residual risk is acceptable. Set the objective before judging the actual result. Use units and populations that can be compared. Make the concern and follow-up responsibility explicit. Target 95% − actual 91% =4 percentage points below target. Slide 3 — Read the comparison—and check the units. Read the comparison—and check the units. The source has three clear percentage comparisons and one row with conflicting units. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Patch Compliance Target 95% · Actual 91% Needs Improvement MFA Adoption Target 100% · Actual 97% Needs Improvement Training Completion Target 95% · Actual 98% On Target Critical Vulnerabilities Image: target<10 · actual 12 · units unstated Source status: Needs Attention. Unit discrepancy: narration says<10%; unscored pending clarification. The original scorecard contains four rows. Patch Compliance 95%/91% and MFA Adoption 100%/97% need improvement; Training Completion 95%/98% meets the target. Critical Vulnerabilities appears as target<10, actual 12 and Needs Attention in the image, but the narration describes the target as less than 10%. This unit discrepancy is retained explicitly rather than silently choosing count or percentage. The fourth row is unscored and cannot support a reliable quantitative decision until the metric owner confirms units, population, time window and intended threshold. The first three rows are course illustrations, not universal policies. Higher can be better for these completion/adoption rates, while other measures may have lower-is-better or range-based objectives; always read the definition. Use the first three rows for unambiguous comparisons. Do not infer the missing unit in the fourth source row. Ask the metric owner to clarify before scoring or deciding. Unclear units are a data-quality finding, not permission to guess. Slide 4 — A report explains the evidence and the action needed. A report explains the evidence and the action needed. Communicate detailed security activities, risks, performance or compliance to a defined audience. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Security incidents Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Vulnerability status Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Risk trends Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Compliance findings Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Control effectiveness Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Security metrics Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Recommended actions Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Cybersecurity reports provide detailed information about activities, risks, performance or compliance. The source lists seven possible topics: incidents, vulnerability status, risk trends, compliance findings, control effectiveness, security metrics and recommended actions. An authored example starts with patch compliance 91% against a95% target, states the scope and unknown critical-system coverage, explains possible business exposure, then recommends validating coverage and assigning remediation owners and due dates. A report should distinguish facts, limitations, interpretations and proposed actions; it should not invent a cause from a single rate. For official AI-related reporting, explain a model-drift KRI with the model/version, baseline, window, validation evidence and responsible owner. A changed indicator warrants review and may have several causes; human decision authority and evidence remain necessary. State scope, period, evidence sources and limitations. Explain the business implication without overstating certainty. Recommend a responsible action, owner and follow-up. Evidence → interpretation with limits → recommended action. Slide 5 — Choose the view for the question being asked. Choose the view for the question being asked. The same evidence can support a dashboard, a scorecard and a report for different purposes. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Metric → Measure Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KPI → Performance Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KRI → Risk Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Dashboard → Visualize Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Scorecard → Compare against targets Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Report → Communicate Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. The source synthesis is Metric→Measure, KPI→Performance, KRI→Risk, Dashboard→Visualize, Scorecard→Compare against targets and Report→Communicate. These are helpful roles, not mutually exclusive software categories. An analyst may need a dashboard to see status and trends, a manager a scorecard to compare actuals with objectives, and a decision-maker a report explaining evidence, risk implications and recommended actions. Choose information based on the question and audience rather than job title alone; a manager can also use a dashboard and a report can include a scorecard. Keep the underlying definitions, units and observation period consistent across views, disclose uncertainty and restrict sensitive detail to authorized recipients. A concise visual view must not conceal a critical exception. Ask whether the need is status, comparison or explanation. Use consistent evidence across the different views. Make the next decision and responsibility visible. Purpose determines the view; evidence supports the decision. Slide 6 — Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Use the clear source patch row: target 95%, actual 91%. Some critical-system coverage is not yet confirmed. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary A Show a dashboard and declare the 95% target met. The actual 91% is below the stated 95% target. Visualization does not change the comparison or prove a cause. B Show the target gap, then explain evidence and propose owner-led follow-up. Use a scorecard for 91% versus 95%, then a report to explain scope, limits, business implications and proposed actions with owners. Do not infer an unproven cause. C Score the ambiguous vulnerability row as a count without checking. The image and narration disagree about units. Keep that row unscored until the definition is clarified. D Hide unknown coverage so the overall status looks healthy. Unknown coverage is a limitation to report and investigate. Concealing it undermines the decision and accountability. This authored scenario applies the source patch-compliance comparison rather than the ambiguous fourth row. The actual 91% is 4 percentage points below 95%. A scorecard answers whether the stated target is met, while a report can explain scope, evidence quality, business implications and recommended follow-up. A dashboard may help visualize the same information, but cannot establish a cause or remove an unknown. Recommend validating critical-system coverage and assigning owners to investigate and remediate with a follow-up date. Do not invent organizational risk acceptance, universal thresholds or an automatic breach conclusion. The fourth source row remains unscored pending clarification of units. Compare actual with the stated target accurately. Communicate unknowns and avoid unsupported causal claims. Recommend accountable follow-up rather than a favourable colour. Make the comparison clear and the follow-up actionable. References & lesson details Before you begin Recommended: previous Domain 2 lessons. Scorecard เทียบผลงานจริงกับเป้าหมาย ตัวอย่างต้นฉบับ: Patch Compliance — เป้า 95% ผลจริง 91% ต้องปรับปรุง แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต เทียบผลงานจริงกับเป้าหมาย ใช้เป้าหมายที่กำหนดก่อนและหลักฐานสอดคล้อง สถานะที่ดีไม่ใช่การประเมินความเสี่ยงทั้งหมด ติดตามความคืบหน้า ใช้เป้าหมายที่กำหนดก่อนและหลักฐานสอดคล้อง สถานะที่ดีไม่ใช่การประเมินความเสี่ยงทั้งหมด ระบุจุดที่น่ากังวล ใช้เป้าหมายที่กำหนดก่อนและหลักฐานสอดคล้อง สถานะที่ดีไม่ใช่การประเมินความเสี่ยงทั้งหมด สื่อสารผลงานให้ผู้บริหาร ใช้เป้าหมายที่กำหนดก่อนและหลักฐานสอดคล้อง สถานะที่ดีไม่ใช่การประเมินความเสี่ยงทั้งหมด สนับสนุน Accountability ใช้เป้าหมายที่กำหนดก่อนและหลักฐานสอดคล้อง สถานะที่ดีไม่ใช่การประเมินความเสี่ยงทั้งหมด Security scorecard สรุปผลงานเทียบวัตถุประสงค์หรือเป้าที่กำหนดไว้ ช่วยเทียบผลจริง ติดตามความคืบหน้า หาจุดกังวล สื่อสารผู้บริหาร และสนับสนุน Accountability ตัวอย่างคอร์สให้ Patch compliance เป้า 95% ผลจริง 91% จึงต้องปรับปรุงเทียบเป้านี้ ช่องว่างคือ 4 Percentage points ไม่ใช่การเปลี่ยนสัมพัทธ์ 4% ค่าเหล่านี้เป็นตัวอย่างองค์กร ไม่ใช่ข้อกำหนด ISC2 หรือเกณฑ์สากล เป้ากับผลจริงต้องใช้ตัววัด งวด และประชากรเดียวกัน ควรระบุเจ้าของกับการติดตามเพื่อให้สถานะนำไปสู่การลงมือ Scorecard อาจใช้สีแต่ต้องมีข้อความชัดด้วย ผ่านเป้าหนึ่งไม่ได้ยืนยันว่าทุก Critical asset ป้องกันครบหรือ Residual risk ยอมรับได้ กำหนดเป้าก่อนตัดสินผลจริง ใช้หน่วยกับประชากรที่เทียบกันได้ บอกจุดกังวลกับผู้รับผิดชอบติดตามให้ชัด เป้า 95% − ผลจริง 91% = ต่ำกว่าเป้า 4 Percentage points Slide 3 — Read the comparison—and check the units. อ่านผลเทียบเป้า และตรวจหน่วยด้วย ต้นฉบับมีสามแถวเปอร์เซ็นต์ที่ชัด และหนึ่งแถวที่หน่วยขัดกัน แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต Patch Compliance เป้า 95% · ผลจริง 91% ต้องปรับปรุง MFA Adoption เป้า 100% · ผลจริง 97% ต้องปรับปรุง Training Completion เป้า 95% · ผลจริง 98% ผ่านเป้า Critical Vulnerabilities ภาพ: เป้า <10 · ผลจริง 12 · ไม่ระบุหน่วย สถานะในภาพ: Needs Attention หน่วยขัดกัน: ผู้บรรยายพูด <10% ไม่ใช้ให้คะแนน รอคำชี้แจง Scorecard เดิมมีสี่แถว Patch Compliance 95%/91% และ MFA Adoption 100%/97% ต้องปรับปรุง ส่วน Training Completion 95%/98% ผ่านเป้า แถว Critical Vulnerabilities ในภาพเป็นเป้า <10 ผลจริง 12 และ Needs Attention แต่เสียงบรรยายบอกเป้าน้อยกว่า 10% จึงเก็บความขัดกันของหน่วยไว้อย่างชัด ไม่เลือกเองว่าเป็นจำนวนหรือเปอร์เซ็นต์ แถวสี่ไม่ใช้ให้คะแนน และยังใช้ตัดสินเชิงปริมาณอย่างเชื่อถือไม่ได้จนเจ้าของ Metric ยืนยันหน่วย ประชากร ช่วงเวลา และเกณฑ์ที่ตั้งใจ สามแถวแรกก็เป็นตัวอย่างคอร์ส ไม่ใช่นโยบายสากล อัตราเรียนครบหรือใช้ MFA เหล่านี้ยิ่งสูงยิ่งดี แต่ตัววัดอื่นอาจยิ่งต่ำยิ่งดีหรือมีช่วงเป้า ต้องอ่านคำนิยามเสมอ ใช้สามแถวแรกเพื่อเทียบที่ชัดเจน อย่าอนุมานหน่วยที่ขาดในแถวสี่ ถามเจ้าของ Metric ให้ชัดก่อนให้คะแนนหรือตัดสินใจ หน่วยไม่ชัดคือข้อพบด้านคุณภาพข้อมูล ไม่ใช่ให้เดา Slide 4 — A report explains the evidence and the action needed. Report อธิบายหลักฐานและสิ่งที่ต้องทำ สื่อสารรายละเอียดกิจกรรม ความเสี่ยง ผลงาน หรือ Compliance ให้ผู้รับที่กำหนด แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต Security incidents อธิบายหลักฐานที่เกี่ยวข้องและความหมายต่อธุรกิจ แยกสิ่งที่สังเกตจริงออกจากการตีความหรือข้อเสนอ สถานะช่องโหว่ อธิบายหลักฐานที่เกี่ยวข้องและความหมายต่อธุรกิจ แยกสิ่งที่สังเกตจริงออกจากการตีความหรือข้อเสนอ แนวโน้มความเสี่ยง อธิบายหลักฐานที่เกี่ยวข้องและความหมายต่อธุรกิจ แยกสิ่งที่สังเกตจริงออกจากการตีความหรือข้อเสนอ ข้อพบ Compliance systems ที่ยังไม่ทราบ อธิบายความเสี่ยงต่อธุรกิจที่อาจมี แล้วแนะนำให้ตรวจความครอบคลุมและมอบหมายเจ้าของแก้ไขพร้อมกำหนดเวลา Report ควรแยกข้อเท็จจริง ข้อจำกัด การตีความ และข้อเสนอ bilingualFields.en: A security scorecard summarizes performance against predefined objectives or targets. It helps compare actual performance, track progress, identify concerns, communicate to management and support accountability. In the course example, patch compliance has a target of 95% and actual 91%, so it needs improvement against that target: a gap of 4 percentage points, not 4% relative change. These are illustrative organizational values, not ISC 2 requirements or universal thresholds. The target and actual must refer to the same measure, period and population; show the owner and follow-up so a status can lead to action. A scorecard may use colours but should also provide explicit text. Meeting one target does not establish that every critical asset is protected or that residual risk is acceptable.

contentModes.info-en: Lesson Info ✕ OBJECTIVE 2.4 Dashboards, Scorecards & Reports What you'll learn Distinguish dashboards, scorecards and reports by the question they answer. Read the source scorecard and communicate uncertainty, including its unit discrepancy. Slides 1–6 — Full explanations Slide 1 — A dashboard makes status and trends visible. A dashboard makes status and trends visible. Choose visual evidence that answers a security question, with a date and a defined scope. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Current security status Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Security incidents Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Vulnerability levels Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Patch compliance Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Risk trends Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. A security dashboard provides a visual representation of cybersecurity information and metrics. The source lists current security status, security incidents, vulnerability levels, patch compliance and risk trends, using charts, graphs, tables or trend indicators. An authored example shows overdue critical findings decreasing from 12 to 8 to 5 across three equal reporting periods; this is a count, not a percentage, and does not alone prove lower overall risk. Define the cohort and investigate missing coverage or changed definitions before interpreting it. A dashboard is not necessarily real time: display its update time and data limitations. For the official AI application, a model-drift KRI can appear alongside other measures, with the model/version, reference population, observation window and responsible reviewer identified. A drift signal prompts validation; it is not automatic proof of an attack or failure. Use a chart, graph, table or trend indicator that supports the question. Keep units, periods and definitions consistent before comparing. Show missing or stale data rather than implying a healthy state. Visible information still needs interpretation. Slide 2 — A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. Source example: Patch Compliance — target 95%, actual 91%, Needs Improvement. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Compare actual performance against targets Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Track progress Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Identify areas of concern Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Communicate performance to management Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Support accountability Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. A security scorecard summarizes performance against predefined objectives or targets. It helps compare actual performance, track progress, identify concerns, communicate to management and support accountability. In the course example, patch compliance has a target of 95% and actual 91%, so it needs improvement against that target: a gap of 4 percentage points, not 4% relative change. These are illustrative organizational values, not ISC 2 requirements or universal thresholds. The target and actual must refer to the same measure, period and population; show the owner and follow-up so a status can lead to action. A scorecard may use colours but should also provide explicit text. Meeting one target does not establish that every critical asset is protected or that residual risk is acceptable. Set the objective before judging the actual result. Use units and populations that can be compared. Make the concern and follow-up responsibility explicit. Target 95% − actual 91% =4 percentage points below target. Slide 3 — Read the comparison—and check the units. Read the comparison—and check the units. The source has three clear percentage comparisons and one row with conflicting units. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Patch Compliance Target 95% · Actual 91% Needs Improvement MFA Adoption Target 100% · Actual 97% Needs Improvement Training Completion Target 95% · Actual 98% On Target Critical Vulnerabilities Image: target<10 · actual 12 · units unstated Source status: Needs Attention. Unit discrepancy: narration says<10%; unscored pending clarification. The original scorecard contains four rows. Patch Compliance 95%/91% and MFA Adoption 100%/97% need improvement; Training Completion 95%/98% meets the target. Critical Vulnerabilities appears as target<10, actual 12 and Needs Attention in the image, but the narration describes the target as less than 10%. This unit discrepancy is retained explicitly rather than silently choosing count or percentage. The fourth row is unscored and cannot support a reliable quantitative decision until the metric owner confirms units, population, time window and intended threshold. The first three rows are course illustrations, not universal policies. Higher can be better for these completion/adoption rates, while other measures may have lower-is-better or range-based objectives; always read the definition. Use the first three rows for unambiguous comparisons. Do not infer the missing unit in the fourth source row. Ask the metric owner to clarify before scoring or deciding. Unclear units are a data-quality finding, not permission to guess. Slide 4 — A report explains the evidence and the action needed. A report explains the evidence and the action needed. Communicate detailed security activities, risks, performance or compliance to a defined audience. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Security incidents Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Vulnerability status Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Risk trends Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Compliance findings Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Control effectiveness Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Security metrics Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Recommended actions Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Cybersecurity reports provide detailed information about activities, risks, performance or compliance. The source lists seven possible topics: incidents, vulnerability status, risk trends, compliance findings, control effectiveness, security metrics and recommended actions. An authored example starts with patch compliance 91% against a95% target, states the scope and unknown critical-system coverage, explains possible business exposure, then recommends validating coverage and assigning remediation owners and due dates. A report should distinguish facts, limitations, interpretations and proposed actions; it should not invent a cause from a single rate. For official AI-related reporting, explain a model-drift KRI with the model/version, baseline, window, validation evidence and responsible owner. A changed indicator warrants review and may have several causes; human decision authority and evidence remain necessary. State scope, period, evidence sources and limitations. Explain the business implication without overstating certainty. Recommend a responsible action, owner and follow-up. Evidence → interpretation with limits → recommended action. Slide 5 — Choose the view for the question being asked. Choose the view for the question being asked. The same evidence can support a dashboard, a scorecard and a report for different purposes. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Metric → Measure Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KPI → Performance Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KRI → Risk Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Dashboard → Visualize Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Scorecard → Compare against targets Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Report → Communicate Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. The source synthesis is Metric→Measure, KPI→Performance, KRI→Risk, Dashboard→Visualize, Scorecard→Compare against targets and Report→Communicate. These are helpful roles, not mutually exclusive software categories. An analyst may need a dashboard to see status and trends, a manager a scorecard to compare actuals with objectives, and a decision-maker a report explaining evidence, risk implications and recommended actions. Choose information based on the question and audience rather than job title alone; a manager can also use a dashboard and a report can include a scorecard. Keep the underlying definitions, units and observation period consistent across views, disclose uncertainty and restrict sensitive detail to authorized recipients. A concise visual view must not conceal a critical exception. Ask whether the need is status, comparison or explanation. Use consistent evidence across the different views. Make the next decision and responsibility visible. Purpose determines the view; evidence supports the decision. Slide 6 — Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Use the clear source patch row: target 95%, actual 91%. Some critical-system coverage is not yet confirmed. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary A Show a dashboard and declare the 95% target met. The actual 91% is below the stated 95% target. Visualization does not change the comparison or prove a cause. B Show the target gap, then explain evidence and propose owner-led follow-up. Use a scorecard for 91% versus 95%, then a report to explain scope, limits, business implications and proposed actions with owners. Do not infer an unproven cause. C Score the ambiguous vulnerability row as a count without checking. The image and narration disagree about units. Keep that row unscored until the definition is clarified. D Hide unknown coverage so the overall status looks healthy. Unknown coverage is a limitation to report and investigate. Concealing it undermines the decision and accountability. This authored scenario applies the source patch-compliance comparison rather than the ambiguous fourth row. The actual 91% is 4 percentage points below 95%. A scorecard answers whether the stated target is met, while a report can explain scope, evidence quality, business implications and recommended follow-up. A dashboard may help visualize the same information, but cannot establish a cause or remove an unknown. Recommend validating critical-system coverage and assigning owners to investigate and remediate with a follow-up date. Do not invent organizational risk acceptance, universal thresholds or an automatic breach conclusion. The fourth source row remains unscored pending clarification of units. Compare actual with the stated target accurately. Communicate unknowns and avoid unsupported causal claims. Recommend accountable follow-up rather than a favourable colour. Make the comparison clear and the follow-up actionable. References & lesson details Before you begin Recommended: previous Domain 2 lessons. contentModes.info-en: Lesson Info ✕ OBJECTIVE 2.4 Dashboards, Scorecards & Reports What you'll learn Distinguish dashboards, scorecards and reports by the question they answer. Read the source scorecard and communicate uncertainty, including its unit discrepancy. Slides 1–6 — Full explanations Slide 1 — A dashboard makes status and trends visible. A dashboard makes status and trends visible. Choose visual evidence that answers a security question, with a date and a defined scope. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Current security status Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Security incidents Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Vulnerability levels Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Patch compliance Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Risk trends Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. A security dashboard provides a visual representation of cybersecurity information and metrics. The source lists current security status, security incidents, vulnerability levels, patch compliance and risk trends, using charts, graphs, tables or trend indicators. An authored example shows overdue critical findings decreasing from 12 to 8 to 5 across three equal reporting periods; this is a count, not a percentage, and does not alone prove lower overall risk. Define the cohort and investigate missing coverage or changed definitions before interpreting it. A dashboard is not necessarily real time: display its update time and data limitations. For the official AI application, a model-drift KRI can appear alongside other measures, with the model/version, reference population, observation window and responsible reviewer identified. A drift signal prompts validation; it is not automatic proof of an attack or failure. Use a chart, graph, table or trend indicator that supports the question. Keep units, periods and definitions consistent before comparing. Show missing or stale data rather than implying a healthy state. Visible information still needs interpretation. Slide 2 — A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. Source example: Patch Compliance — target 95%, actual 91%, Needs Improvement. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Compare actual performance against targets Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Track progress Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Identify areas of concern Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Communicate performance to management Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Support accountability Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. A security scorecard summarizes performance against predefined objectives or targets. It helps compare actual performance, track progress, identify concerns, communicate to management and support accountability. In the course example, patch compliance has a target of 95% and actual 91%, so it needs improvement against that target: a gap of 4 percentage points, not 4% relative change. These are illustrative organizational values, not ISC 2 requirements or universal thresholds. The target and actual must refer to the same measure, period and population; show the owner and follow-up so a status can lead to action. A scorecard may use colours but should also provide explicit text. Meeting one target does not establish that every critical asset is protected or that residual risk is acceptable. Set the objective before judging the actual result. Use units and populations that can be compared. Make the concern and follow-up responsibility explicit. Target 95% − actual 91% =4 percentage points below target. Slide 3 — Read the comparison—and check the units. Read the comparison—and check the units. The source has three clear percentage comparisons and one row with conflicting units. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Patch Compliance Target 95% · Actual 91% Needs Improvement MFA Adoption Target 100% · Actual 97% Needs Improvement Training Completion Target 95% · Actual 98% On Target Critical Vulnerabilities Image: target<10 · actual 12 · units unstated Source status: Needs Attention. Unit discrepancy: narration says<10%; unscored pending clarification. The original scorecard contains four rows. Patch Compliance 95%/91% and MFA Adoption 100%/97% need improvement; Training Completion 95%/98% meets the target. Critical Vulnerabilities appears as target<10, actual 12 and Needs Attention in the image, but the narration describes the target as less than 10%. This unit discrepancy is retained explicitly rather than silently choosing count or percentage. The fourth row is unscored and cannot support a reliable quantitative decision until the metric owner confirms units, population, time window and intended threshold. The first three rows are course illustrations, not universal policies. Higher can be better for these completion/adoption rates, while other measures may have lower-is-better or range-based objectives; always read the definition. Use the first three rows for unambiguous comparisons. Do not infer the missing unit in the fourth source row. Ask the metric owner to clarify before scoring or deciding. Unclear units are a data-quality finding, not permission to guess. Slide 4 — A report explains the evidence and the action needed. A report explains the evidence and the action needed. Communicate detailed security activities, risks, performance or compliance to a defined audience. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Security incidents Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Vulnerability status Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Risk trends Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Compliance findings Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Control effectiveness Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Security metrics Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Recommended actions Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Cybersecurity reports provide detailed information about activities, risks, performance or compliance. The source lists seven possible topics: incidents, vulnerability status, risk trends, compliance findings, control effectiveness, security metrics and recommended actions. An authored example starts with patch compliance 91% against a95% target, states the scope and unknown critical-system coverage, explains possible business exposure, then recommends validating coverage and assigning remediation owners and due dates. A report should distinguish facts, limitations, interpretations and proposed actions; it should not invent a cause from a single rate. For official AI-related reporting, explain a model-drift KRI with the model/version, baseline, window, validation evidence and responsible owner. A changed indicator warrants review and may have several causes; human decision authority and evidence remain necessary. State scope, period, evidence sources and limitations. Explain the business implication without overstating certainty. Recommend a responsible action, owner and follow-up. Evidence → interpretation with limits → recommended action. Slide 5 — Choose the view for the question being asked. Choose the view for the question being asked. The same evidence can support a dashboard, a scorecard and a report for different purposes. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Metric → Measure Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KPI → Performance Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KRI → Risk Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Dashboard → Visualize Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Scorecard → Compare against targets Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Report → Communicate Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. The source synthesis is Metric→Measure, KPI→Performance, KRI→Risk, Dashboard→Visualize, Scorecard→Compare against targets and Report→Communicate. These are helpful roles, not mutually exclusive software categories. An analyst may need a dashboard to see status and trends, a manager a scorecard to compare actuals with objectives, and a decision-maker a report explaining evidence, risk implications and recommended actions. Choose information based on the question and audience rather than job title alone; a manager can also use a dashboard and a report can include a scorecard. Keep the underlying definitions, units and observation period consistent across views, disclose uncertainty and restrict sensitive detail to authorized recipients. A concise visual view must not conceal a critical exception. Ask whether the need is status, comparison or explanation. Use consistent evidence across the different views. Make the next decision and responsibility visible. Purpose determines the view; evidence supports the decision. Slide 6 — Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Use the clear source patch row: target 95%, actual 91%. Some critical-system coverage is not yet confirmed. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary A Show a dashboard and declare the 95% target met. The actual 91% is below the stated 95% target. Visualization does not change the comparison or prove a cause. B Show the target gap, then explain evidence and propose owner-led follow-up. Use a scorecard for 91% versus 95%, then a report to explain scope, limits, business implications and proposed actions with owners. Do not infer an unproven cause. C Score the ambiguous vulnerability row as a count without checking. The image and narration disagree about units. Keep that row unscored until the definition is clarified. D Hide unknown coverage so the overall status looks healthy. Unknown coverage is a limitation to report and investigate. Concealing it undermines the decision and accountability. This authored scenario applies the source patch-compliance comparison rather than the ambiguous fourth row. The actual 91% is 4 percentage points below 95%. A scorecard answers whether the stated target is met, while a report can explain scope, evidence quality, business implications and recommended follow-up. A dashboard may help visualize the same information, but cannot establish a cause or remove an unknown. Recommend validating critical-system coverage and assigning owners to investigate and remediate with a follow-up date. Do not invent organizational risk acceptance, universal thresholds or an automatic breach conclusion. The fourth source row remains unscored pending clarification of units. Compare actual with the stated target accurately. Communicate unknowns and avoid unsupported causal claims. Recommend accountable follow-up rather than a favourable colour. bilingualFields.en: Cybersecurity reports provide detailed information about activities, risks, performance or compliance. The source lists seven possible topics: incidents, vulnerability status, risk trends, compliance findings, control effectiveness, security metrics and recommended actions. An authored example starts with patch compliance 91% against a95% target, states the scope and unknown critical-system coverage, explains possible business exposure, then recommends validating coverage and assigning remediation owners and due dates. A report should distinguish facts, limitations, interpretations and proposed actions; it should not invent a cause from a single rate. For official AI-related reporting, explain a model-drift KRI with the model/version, baseline, window, validation evidence and responsible owner. A changed indicator warrants review and may have several causes; human decision authority and evidence remain necessary.

contentModes.info-en: Lesson Info ✕ OBJECTIVE 2.4 Dashboards, Scorecards & Reports What you'll learn Distinguish dashboards, scorecards and reports by the question they answer. Read the source scorecard and communicate uncertainty, including its unit discrepancy. Slides 1–6 — Full explanations Slide 1 — A dashboard makes status and trends visible. A dashboard makes status and trends visible. Choose visual evidence that answers a security question, with a date and a defined scope. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Current security status Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Security incidents Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Vulnerability levels Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Patch compliance Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Risk trends Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. A security dashboard provides a visual representation of cybersecurity information and metrics. The source lists current security status, security incidents, vulnerability levels, patch compliance and risk trends, using charts, graphs, tables or trend indicators. An authored example shows overdue critical findings decreasing from 12 to 8 to 5 across three equal reporting periods; this is a count, not a percentage, and does not alone prove lower overall risk. Define the cohort and investigate missing coverage or changed definitions before interpreting it. A dashboard is not necessarily real time: display its update time and data limitations. For the official AI application, a model-drift KRI can appear alongside other measures, with the model/version, reference population, observation window and responsible reviewer identified. A drift signal prompts validation; it is not automatic proof of an attack or failure. Use a chart, graph, table or trend indicator that supports the question. Keep units, periods and definitions consistent before comparing. Show missing or stale data rather than implying a healthy state. Visible information still needs interpretation. Slide 2 — A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. Source example: Patch Compliance — target 95%, actual 91%, Needs Improvement. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Compare actual performance against targets Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Track progress Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Identify areas of concern Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Communicate performance to management Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Support accountability Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. A security scorecard summarizes performance against predefined objectives or targets. It helps compare actual performance, track progress, identify concerns, communicate to management and support accountability. In the course example, patch compliance has a target of 95% and actual 91%, so it needs improvement against that target: a gap of 4 percentage points, not 4% relative change. These are illustrative organizational values, not ISC 2 requirements or universal thresholds. The target and actual must refer to the same measure, period and population; show the owner and follow-up so a status can lead to action. A scorecard may use colours but should also provide explicit text. Meeting one target does not establish that every critical asset is protected or that residual risk is acceptable. Set the objective before judging the actual result. Use units and populations that can be compared. Make the concern and follow-up responsibility explicit. Target 95% − actual 91% =4 percentage points below target. Slide 3 — Read the comparison—and check the units. Read the comparison—and check the units. The source has three clear percentage comparisons and one row with conflicting units. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Patch Compliance Target 95% · Actual 91% Needs Improvement MFA Adoption Target 100% · Actual 97% Needs Improvement Training Completion Target 95% · Actual 98% On Target Critical Vulnerabilities Image: target<10 · actual 12 · units unstated Source status: Needs Attention. Unit discrepancy: narration says<10%; unscored pending clarification. The original scorecard contains four rows. Patch Compliance 95%/91% and MFA Adoption 100%/97% need improvement; Training Completion 95%/98% meets the target. Critical Vulnerabilities appears as target<10, actual 12 and Needs Attention in the image, but the narration describes the target as less than 10%. This unit discrepancy is retained explicitly rather than silently choosing count or percentage. The fourth row is unscored and cannot support a reliable quantitative decision until the metric owner confirms units, population, time window and intended threshold. The first three rows are course illustrations, not universal policies. Higher can be better for these completion/adoption rates, while other measures may have lower-is-better or range-based objectives; always read the definition. Use the first three rows for unambiguous comparisons. Do not infer the missing unit in the fourth source row. Ask the metric owner to clarify before scoring or deciding. Unclear units are a data-quality finding, not permission to guess. Slide 4 — A report explains the evidence and the action needed. A report explains the evidence and the action needed. For official AI-related reporting, explain a model-drift KRI with the model/version, baseline, window, validation evidence and responsible owner. A changed indicator warrants review and may have several causes; human decision authority and evidence remain necessary. State scope, period, evidence sources and limitations. Explain the business implication without overstating certainty. Recommend a responsible action, owner and follow-up. Evidence → interpretation with limits → recommended action. Slide 5 — Choose the view for the question being asked. Choose the view for the question being asked. The same evidence can support a dashboard, a scorecard and a report for different purposes. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Metric → Measure Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KPI → Performance Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KRI → Risk Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Dashboard → Visualize Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Scorecard → Compare against targets Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Report → Communicate Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. The source synthesis is Metric→Measure, KPI→Performance, KRI→Risk, Dashboard→Visualize, Scorecard→Compare against targets and Report→Communicate. These are helpful roles, not mutually exclusive software categories. An analyst may need a dashboard to see status and trends, a manager a scorecard to compare actuals with objectives, and a decision-maker a report explaining evidence, risk implications and recommended actions. Choose information based on the question and audience rather than job title alone; a manager can also use a dashboard and a report can include a scorecard. Keep the underlying definitions, units and observation period consistent across views, disclose uncertainty and restrict sensitive detail to authorized recipients. A concise visual view must not conceal a critical exception. Ask whether the need is status, comparison or explanation. Use consistent evidence across the different views. Make the next decision and responsibility visible. Purpose determines the view; evidence supports the decision. Slide 6 — Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Use the clear source patch row: target 95%, actual 91%. Some critical-system coverage is not yet confirmed. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary A Show a dashboard and declare the 95% target met. The actual 91% is below the stated 95% target. Visualization does not change the comparison or prove a cause. B Show the target gap, then explain evidence and propose owner-led follow-up. Use a scorecard for 91% versus 95%, then a report to explain scope, limits, business implications and proposed actions with owners. Do not infer an unproven cause. C Score the ambiguous vulnerability row as a count without checking. The image and narration disagree about units. Keep that row unscored until the definition is clarified. D Hide unknown coverage so the overall status looks healthy. Unknown coverage is a limitation to report and investigate. Concealing it undermines the decision and accountability. This authored scenario applies the source patch-compliance comparison rather than the ambiguous fourth row. The actual 91% is 4 percentage points below 95%. A scorecard answers whether the stated target is met, while a report can explain scope, evidence quality, business implications and recommended follow-up. A dashboard may help visualize the same information, but cannot establish a cause or remove an unknown. Recommend validating critical-system coverage and assigning owners to investigate and remediate with a follow-up date. Do not invent organizational risk acceptance, universal thresholds or an automatic breach conclusion. The fourth source row remains unscored pending clarification of units. Compare actual with the stated target accurately. Communicate unknowns and avoid unsupported causal claims. Recommend accountable follow-up rather than a favourable colour. Make the comparison clear and the follow-up actionable. References & lesson details Before you begin Recommended: previous Domain 2 lessons. contentModes.info-th: Lesson Info ✕ OBJECTIVE 2.4 Dashboard, Scorecard และ Report What you'll learn แยก Dashboard, Scorecard และ Report ตามคำถามที่ตอบ อ่าน Scorecard ต้นฉบับและสื่อสารความไม่แน่นอน รวมหน่วยที่ขัดกัน Slides 1–6 — Full explanations Slide 1 — A dashboard makes status and trends visible. Dashboard ช่วยให้เห็นสถานะและแนวโน้ม เลือกภาพหลักฐานที่ตอบคำถาม Security พร้อมวันวัดและขอบเขตชัดเจน แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต สถานะ Security ปัจจุบัน แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล Security incidents แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล ระดับช่องโหว่ แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล Patch compliance แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล แนวโน้มความเสี่ยง แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล Security dashboard แสดงข้อมูลและ Metric ด้าน Cybersecurity เป็นภาพ ต้นฉบับระบุสถานะปัจจุบัน Incident ระดับช่องโหว่ Patch compliance และแนวโน้มความเสี่ยง โดยอาจใช้ Chart, Graph, Table หรือ Trend indicator ตัวอย่างแต่งแสดงรายการ Critical เกินกำหนดลดจาก 12 เป็น 8 เป็น 5 ในสามงวดเท่ากัน ค่านี้เป็นจำนวน ไม่ใช่เปอร์เซ็นต์ และไม่ได้พิสูจน์ว่าความเสี่ยงรวมลด ต้องกำหนดกลุ่มรายการ ตรวจความครอบคลุมที่หายหรือคำนิยามที่เปลี่ยนก่อนตีความ Dashboard ไม่จำเป็นต้องเป็น Real time ให้แสดงเวลาอัปเดตกับข้อจำกัดข้อมูล ตาม AI application ใน Outline อาจแสดง Model-drift KRI ร่วมกับตัววัดอื่น โดยระบุ Model/Version ประชากรอ้างอิง ช่วงสังเกต และผู้ทบทวน สัญญาณ Drift ให้ตรวจสอบ ไม่ใช่หลักฐานอัตโนมัติว่าโจมตีหรือระบบล้มเหลว ใช้ Chart, Graph, Table หรือ Trend indicator ให้ตอบคำถาม ใช้หน่วย งวด และคำนิยามสอดคล้องก่อนเทียบ แสดงข้อมูลที่หายหรือล้าสมัย ไม่สื่อว่าปลอดภัยโดยปริยาย เห็นข้อมูลแล้วก็ยังต้องตีความ Slide 2 — A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. Scorecard เทียบผลงานจริงกับเป้าหมาย ตัวอย่างต้นฉบับ: Patch Compliance — เป้า 95% ผลจริง 91% ต้องปรับปรุง แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต ผลจริง 91% จึงต้องปรับปรุงเทียบเป้านี้ ช่องว่างคือ 4 Percentage points ไม่ใช่การเปลี่ยนสัมพัทธ์ 4% ค่าเหล่านี้เป็นตัวอย่างองค์กร ไม่ใช่ข้อกำหนด ISC2 หรือเกณฑ์สากล เป้ากับผลจริงต้องใช้ตัววัด งวด และประชากรเดียวกัน ควรระบุเจ้าของกับการติดตามเพื่อให้สถานะนำไปสู่การลงมือ Scorecard อาจใช้สีแต่ต้องมีข้อความชัดด้วย ผ่านเป้าหนึ่งไม่ได้ยืนยันว่าทุก Critical asset ป้องกันครบหรือ Residual risk ยอมรับได้ กำหนดเป้าก่อนตัดสินผลจริง ใช้หน่วยกับประชากรที่เทียบกันได้ บอกจุดกังวลกับผู้รับผิดชอบติดตามให้ชัด เป้า 95% − ผลจริง 91% = ต่ำกว่าเป้า 4 Percentage points Slide 3 — Read the comparison—and check the units. อ่านผลเทียบเป้า และตรวจหน่วยด้วย ต้นฉบับมีสามแถวเปอร์เซ็นต์ที่ชัด และหนึ่งแถวที่หน่วยขัดกัน แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต Patch ไม่เลือกเองว่าเป็นจำนวนหรือเปอร์เซ็นต์ แถวสี่ไม่ใช้ให้คะแนน และยังใช้ตัดสินเชิงปริมาณอย่างเชื่อถือไม่ได้จนเจ้าของ Metric ยืนยันหน่วย ประชากร ช่วงเวลา และเกณฑ์ที่ตั้งใจ สามแถวแรกก็เป็นตัวอย่างคอร์ส contentModes.info-en: Lesson Info ✕ OBJECTIVE 2.4 Dashboards, Scorecards & Reports What you'll learn Distinguish dashboards, scorecards and reports by the question they answer. Read the source scorecard and communicate uncertainty, including its unit discrepancy. Slides 1–6 — Full explanations Slide 1 — A dashboard makes status and trends visible. A dashboard makes status and trends visible. Choose visual evidence that answers a security question, with a date and a defined scope. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Current security status Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Security incidents Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Vulnerability levels Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Patch compliance Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. Risk trends Visualize relevant measures State the source, population and update time. A security dashboard provides a visual representation of cybersecurity information and metrics. The source lists current security status, security incidents, vulnerability levels, patch compliance and risk trends, using charts, graphs, tables or trend indicators. An authored example shows overdue critical findings decreasing from 12 to 8 to 5 across three equal reporting periods; this is a count, not a percentage, and does not alone prove lower overall risk. Define the cohort and investigate missing coverage or changed definitions before interpreting it. A dashboard is not necessarily real time: display its update time and data limitations. For the official AI application, a model-drift KRI can appear alongside other measures, with the model/version, reference population, observation window and responsible reviewer identified. A drift signal prompts validation; it is not automatic proof of an attack or failure. Use a chart, graph, table or trend indicator that supports the question. Keep units, periods and definitions consistent before comparing. Show missing or stale data rather than implying a healthy state. Visible information still needs interpretation. Slide 2 — A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. Source example: Patch Compliance — target 95%, actual 91%, Needs Improvement. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Compare actual performance against targets Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Track progress Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Identify areas of concern Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Communicate performance to management Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. Support accountability Use a predefined objective and consistent evidence A favourable status is not a complete risk assessment. A security scorecard summarizes performance against predefined objectives or targets. It helps compare actual performance, track progress, identify concerns, communicate to management and support accountability. In the course example, patch compliance has a target of 95% and actual 91%, so it needs improvement against that target: a gap of 4 percentage points, not 4% relative change. These are illustrative organizational values, not ISC 2 requirements or universal thresholds. The target and actual must refer to the same measure, period and population; show the owner and follow-up so a status can lead to action. A scorecard may use colours but should also provide explicit text. Meeting one target does not establish that every critical asset is protected or that residual risk is acceptable. Set the objective before judging the actual result. Use units and populations that can be compared. Make the concern and follow-up responsibility explicit. Target 95% − actual 91% =4 percentage points below target. Slide 3 — Read the comparison—and check the units. Read the comparison—and check the units. The source has three clear percentage comparisons and one row with conflicting units. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Patch Compliance Target 95% · Actual 91% Needs Improvement MFA Adoption Target 100% · Actual 97% Needs Improvement Training Completion Target 95% · Actual 98% On Target Critical Vulnerabilities Image: target<10 · actual 12 · units unstated Source status: Needs Attention. Unit discrepancy: narration says<10%; unscored pending clarification. The original scorecard contains four rows. Patch Compliance 95%/91% and MFA Adoption 100%/97% need improvement; Training Completion 95%/98% meets the target. Critical Vulnerabilities appears as target<10, actual 12 and Needs Attention in the image, but the narration describes the target as less than 10%. This unit discrepancy is retained explicitly rather than silently choosing count or percentage. The fourth row is unscored and cannot support a reliable quantitative decision until the metric owner confirms units, population, time window and intended threshold. The first three rows are course illustrations, not universal policies. Higher can be better for these completion/adoption rates, while other measures may have lower-is-better or range-based objectives; always read the definition. Use the first three rows for unambiguous comparisons. Do not infer the missing unit in the fourth source row. Ask the metric owner to clarify before scoring or deciding. Unclear units are a data-quality finding, not permission to guess. Slide 4 — A report explains the evidence and the action needed. A report explains the evidence and the action needed. Communicate detailed security activities, risks, performance or compliance to a defined audience. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Security incidents Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Vulnerability status Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Risk trends Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Compliance findings Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Control effectiveness Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Security metrics Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Recommended actions Explain relevant evidence and business meaning Distinguish an observed fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Cybersecurity reports provide detailed information about activities, risks, performance or compliance. The source lists seven possible topics: incidents, vulnerability status, risk trends, compliance findings, control effectiveness, security metrics and recommended actions. An authored example starts with patch compliance 91% against a95% target, states the scope and unknown critical-system coverage, explains possible business exposure, then recommends validating coverage and assigning remediation owners and due dates. A report should distinguish facts, limitations, interpretations and proposed actions; it should not invent a cause from a single rate. For official AI-related reporting, explain a model-drift KRI with the model/version, baseline, window, validation evidence and responsible owner. A changed indicator warrants review and may have several causes; human decision authority and evidence remain necessary. State scope, period, evidence sources and limitations. Explain the business implication without overstating certainty. Recommend a responsible action, owner and follow-up. Evidence → interpretation with limits → recommended action. Slide 5 — Choose the view for the question being asked. Choose the view for the question being asked. The same evidence can support a dashboard, a scorecard and a report for different purposes. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary Metric → Measure Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KPI → Performance Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. KRI → Risk Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Dashboard → Visualize Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Scorecard → Compare against targets Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. Report → Communicate Use the term according to its purpose These roles can appear together in one product. The source synthesis is Metric→Measure, KPI→Performance, KRI→Risk, Dashboard→Visualize, Scorecard→Compare against targets and Report→Communicate. These are helpful roles, not mutually exclusive software categories. An analyst may need a dashboard to see status and trends, a manager a scorecard to compare actuals with objectives, and a decision-maker a report explaining evidence, risk implications and recommended actions. Choose information based on the question and audience rather than job title alone; a manager can also use a dashboard and a report can include a scorecard. Keep the underlying definitions, units and observation period consistent across views, disclose uncertainty and restrict sensitive detail to authorized recipients. A concise visual view must not conceal a critical exception. Ask whether the need is status, comparison or explanation. Use consistent evidence across the different views. Make the next decision and responsibility visible. Purpose determines the view; evidence supports the decision. Slide 6 — Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Management asks: are we on target, and what should happen next? Use the clear source patch row: target 95%, actual 91%. Some critical-system coverage is not yet confirmed. Concepts and practical reasoning Concept / action Meaning / application Reason / boundary A Show a dashboard and declare the 95% target met. The actual 91% is below the stated 95% target. Visualization does not change the comparison or prove a cause. B Show the target gap, then explain evidence and propose owner-led follow-up. Use a scorecard for 91% versus 95%, then a report to explain scope, limits, business implications and proposed actions with owners. Do not infer an unproven cause. C Score the ambiguous vulnerability row as a count without checking. The image and narration disagree about units. Keep that row unscored until the definition is clarified. D Hide unknown coverage so the overall status looks healthy. Unknown coverage is a limitation to report and investigate. Concealing it undermines the decision and accountability. This authored scenario applies the source patch-compliance comparison rather than the ambiguous fourth row. The actual 91% is 4 percentage points below 95%. A scorecard answers whether the stated target is met, while a report can explain scope, evidence quality, business implications and recommended follow-up. A dashboard may help visualize the same information, but cannot establish a cause or remove an unknown. Recommend validating critical-system coverage and assigning owners to investigate and remediate with a follow-up date. Do not invent organizational risk acceptance, universal thresholds or an automatic breach conclusion. The fourth source row remains unscored pending clarification of units. Compare actual with the stated target accurately. Communicate unknowns and avoid unsupported causal claims. Recommend accountable follow-up rather than a favourable colour. Make the comparison clear and the follow-up actionable. References & lesson details Before you begin Recommended: previous Domain 2 lessons. contentModes.info-th: Lesson Info ✕ OBJECTIVE 2.4 Dashboard, Scorecard และ Report What you'll learn แยก Dashboard, Scorecard และ Report ตามคำถามที่ตอบ อ่าน Scorecard ต้นฉบับและสื่อสารความไม่แน่นอน รวมหน่วยที่ขัดกัน Slides 1–6 — Full explanations Slide 1 — A dashboard makes status and trends visible. Dashboard ช่วยให้เห็นสถานะและแนวโน้ม เลือกภาพหลักฐานที่ตอบคำถาม Security พร้อมวันวัดและขอบเขตชัดเจน แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต สถานะ Security ปัจจุบัน แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล Security incidents แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล ระดับช่องโหว่ แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล Patch compliance แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล แนวโน้มความเสี่ยง แสดงตัววัดที่เกี่ยวข้องเป็นภาพ ระบุแหล่งข้อมูล ประชากร และเวลาปรับข้อมูล Security dashboard แสดงข้อมูลและ Metric ด้าน Cybersecurity เป็นภาพ ต้นฉบับระบุสถานะปัจจุบัน Incident ระดับช่องโหว่ Patch compliance และแนวโน้มความเสี่ยง โดยอาจใช้ Chart, Graph, Table หรือ Trend indicator ตัวอย่างแต่งแสดงรายการ Critical เกินกำหนดลดจาก 12 เป็น 8 เป็น 5 ในสามงวดเท่ากัน ค่านี้เป็นจำนวน ไม่ใช่เปอร์เซ็นต์ และไม่ได้พิสูจน์ว่าความเสี่ยงรวมลด ต้องกำหนดกลุ่มรายการ ตรวจความครอบคลุมที่หายหรือคำนิยามที่เปลี่ยนก่อนตีความ Dashboard ไม่จำเป็นต้องเป็น Real time ให้แสดงเวลาอัปเดตกับข้อจำกัดข้อมูล ตาม AI application ใน Outline อาจแสดง Model-drift KRI ร่วมกับตัววัดอื่น โดยระบุ Model/Version ประชากรอ้างอิง ช่วงสังเกต และผู้ทบทวน สัญญาณ Drift ให้ตรวจสอบ ไม่ใช่หลักฐานอัตโนมัติว่าโจมตีหรือระบบล้มเหลว ใช้ Chart, Graph, Table หรือ Trend indicator ให้ตอบคำถาม ใช้หน่วย งวด และคำนิยามสอดคล้องก่อนเทียบ แสดงข้อมูลที่หายหรือล้าสมัย ไม่สื่อว่าปลอดภัยโดยปริยาย เห็นข้อมูลแล้วก็ยังต้องตีความ Slide 2 — A scorecard compares actual performance with a target. Scorecard เทียบผลงานจริงกับเป้าหมาย ตัวอย่างต้นฉบับ: Patch Compliance — เป้า 95% ผลจริง 91% ต้องปรับปรุง แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต สถานะที่ดีไม่ใช่การประเมินความเสี่ยงทั้งหมด ระบุจุดที่น่ากังวล ใช้เป้าหมายที่กำหนดก่อนและหลักฐานสอดคล้อง สถานะที่ดีไม่ใช่การประเมินความเสี่ยงทั้งหมด สื่อสารผลงานให้ผู้บริหาร Security scorecard สรุปผลงานเทียบวัตถุประสงค์หรือเป้าที่กำหนดไว้ ช่วยเทียบผลจริง ติดตามความคืบหน้า หาจุดกังวล สื่อสารผู้บริหาร และสนับสนุน Accountability ตัวอย่างคอร์สให้ Patch compliance เป้า 95% ผลจริง 91% จึงต้องปรับปรุงเทียบเป้านี้ ช่องว่างคือ 4 Percentage points ไม่ใช่การเปลี่ยนสัมพัทธ์ 4% ค่าเหล่านี้เป็นตัวอย่างองค์กร ไม่ใช่ข้อกำหนด ISC2 หรือเกณฑ์สากล เป้ากับผลจริงต้องใช้ตัววัด งวด และประชากรเดียวกัน ควรระบุเจ้าของกับการติดตามเพื่อให้สถานะนำไปสู่การลงมือ Scorecard อาจใช้สีแต่ต้องมีข้อความชัดด้วย ผ่านเป้าหนึ่งไม่ได้ยืนยันว่าทุก Critical asset ป้องกันครบหรือ Residual risk ยอมรับได้ กำหนดเป้าก่อนตัดสินผลจริง ใช้หน่วยกับประชากรที่เทียบกันได้ บอกจุดกังวลกับผู้รับผิดชอบติดตามให้ชัด เป้า 95% − ผลจริง 91% = ต่ำกว่าเป้า 4 Percentage points Slide 3 — Read the comparison—and check the units. อ่านผลเทียบเป้า และตรวจหน่วยด้วย ต้นฉบับมีสามแถวเปอร์เซ็นต์ที่ชัด และหนึ่งแถวที่หน่วยขัดกัน แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต Patch Compliance เป้า 95% · ผลจริง 91% ต้องปรับปรุง MFA Adoption เป้า 100% · ผลจริง 97% ต้องปรับปรุง Training Completion เป้า 95% · ผลจริง 98% ผ่านเป้า Critical Vulnerabilities ภาพ: เป้า <10 · ผลจริง 12 · Completion 95%/98% ผ่านเป้า แถว Critical Vulnerabilities ในภาพเป็นเป้า <10 ผลจริง 12 และ Needs Attention แต่เสียงบรรยายบอกเป้าน้อยกว่า 10% จึงเก็บความขัดกันของหน่วยไว้อย่างชัด ไม่เลือกเองว่าเป็นจำนวนหรือเปอร์เซ็นต์ แถวสี่ไม่ใช้ให้คะแนน และยังใช้ตัดสินเชิงปริมาณอย่างเชื่อถือไม่ได้จนเจ้าของ Metric ยืนยันหน่วย ประชากร ช่วงเวลา และเกณฑ์ที่ตั้งใจ สามแถวแรกก็เป็นตัวอย่างคอร์ส ไม่ใช่นโยบายสากล อัตราเรียนครบหรือใช้ MFA เหล่านี้ยิ่งสูงยิ่งดี แต่ตัววัดอื่นอาจยิ่งต่ำยิ่งดีหรือมีช่วงเป้า ต้องอ่านคำนิยามเสมอ ใช้สามแถวแรกเพื่อเทียบที่ชัดเจน อย่าอนุมานหน่วยที่ขาดในแถวสี่ ถามเจ้าของ Metric ให้ชัดก่อนให้คะแนนหรือตัดสินใจ หน่วยไม่ชัดคือข้อพบด้านคุณภาพข้อมูล ไม่ใช่ให้เดา Slide 4 — A report explains the evidence and the action needed. Scorecard→Compare against targets และ Report→Communicate คำเหล่านี้ช่วยจำบทบาท ไม่ใช่ประเภท Software ที่แยกขาดกัน นักวิเคราะห์อาจต้องการ Dashboard ดูสถานะ/แนวโน้ม ผู้จัดการใช้ Scorecard เทียบเป้า และควรทำอะไรต่อ? ใช้แถว Patch ที่ชัด: เป้า 95% ผลจริง 91% และยังยืนยันความครอบคลุมระบบสำคัญบางส่วนไม่ได้ แนวคิดและเหตุผลในการปฏิบัติ แนวคิด / แนวทาง ความหมาย / การใช้ เหตุผล / ขอบเขต A แสดง Dashboard แล้วประกาศว่าผ่านเป้า 95% ผลจริง 91% ต่ำกว่าเป้า 95% การแสดงเป็นภาพไม่เปลี่ยนผลเทียบหรือพิสูจน์สาเหตุ B แสดงช่องว่างเป้า แล้วอธิบายหลักฐานและเสนอเจ้าของติดตาม ใช้ Scorecard เทียบ 91% กับ 95% แล้วใช้ Report อธิบายขอบเขต ข้อจำกัด ผลต่อธุรกิจ และข้อเสนอพร้อมเจ้าของ อย่าสรุปสาเหตุที่ยังไม่พิสูจน์ C ให้คะแนนแถวช่องโหว่ที่หน่วยขัดกันว่าเป็นจำนวนโดยไม่ตรวจ ภาพกับเสียงบรรยายหน่วยไม่ตรงกัน ต้องไม่ใช้แถวนั้นให้คะแนนจนคำนิยามชัด D ซ่อนความครอบคลุมที่ไม่ทราบให้ภาพรวมดูดี ความครอบคลุมที่ไม่ทราบเป็นข้อจำกัดที่ต้องรายงานและตรวจ การซ่อนทำลายการตัดสินใจและ Accountability สถานการณ์แต่งนี้ใช้ผลเทียบ Patch compliance จากต้นฉบับ ไม่ใช้แถวสี่ที่หน่วยขัดกัน ผลจริง 91% ต่ำกว่า 95% อยู่ 4 Percentage points Scorecard ตอบว่าผ่านเป้าที่ระบุหรือไม่ ส่วน Report อธิบายขอบเขต คุณภาพหลักฐาน ผลต่อธุรกิจ และแนวทางติดตามได้ Dashboard อาจช่วยแสดงข้อมูลเดียวกันเป็นภาพ แต่พิสูจน์สาเหตุหรือทำให้สิ่งไม่ทราบหายไปไม่ได้ ควรตรวจความครอบคลุมระบบสำคัญ แล้วมอบหมายเจ้าของตรวจ/แก้ไขพร้อมวันติดตาม ไม่สร้างข้อสรุปว่าองค์กรยอมรับความเสี่ยง เกณฑ์สากล หรือเกิด Breach อัตโนมัติ แถวสี่ต้นฉบับยังไม่ให้คะแนนจนยืนยันหน่วย เทียบผลจริงกับเป้าที่ระบุให้ถูก สื่อสารสิ่งไม่ทราบ ไม่อ้างสาเหตุเกินหลักฐาน เสนอการติดตามที่มีเจ้าของ ไม่ใช่แค่สีที่ดูดี ทำผลเทียบให้ชัด และให้ข้อเสนอนำไปทำต่อได้ References & lesson details Before you begin bilingualFields.en: This authored scenario applies the source patch-compliance comparison rather than the ambiguous fourth row. The actual 91% is 4 percentage points below 95%. A scorecard answers whether the stated target is met, while a report can explain scope, evidence quality, business implications and recommended follow-up. A dashboard may help visualize the same information, but cannot establish a cause or remove an unknown. Recommend validating critical-system coverage and assigning owners to investigate and remediate with a follow-up date. Do not invent organizational risk acceptance, universal thresholds or an automatic breach conclusion. The fourth source row remains unscored pending clarification of units.
